title: Are Your Performance Measures Current?
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece challenges leaders to audit whether the performance metrics guiding their organization have kept pace with how much the organization itself has changed. It observes that many enterprises still track the same KPIs and OKRs they used a decade ago, even though the environment, priorities, and challenges driving success have shifted substantially in that time. The article argues stale metrics don't just fail to help — they actively obscure the real picture of organizational effectiveness, leading leaders to make decisions on outdated signals. It closes with a direct challenge to readers to check whether their own metrics have changed recently, framing metric freshness as a first-order strategic responsibility.
points: The article's central challenge is whether an organization's KPIs and OKRs have evolved as fast as the organization itself has changed.
It observes that many enterprises are still tracking the same primary metrics they used a decade ago, despite significant environmental and organizational change since then.
Stale metrics are framed as actively harmful, not merely unhelpful — they obscure the real picture and lead to decisions based on outdated signals.
The piece closes by framing metric freshness as a "first strategic mandate," elevating it above a routine administrative task.
quotes: A question every organization and leader should ask is how current their metrics really are.
Too many organizations and leaders don’t update the metrics they use to keep pace with the changes they experience.
If the performance measurements don’t evolve with the enterprise, leaders are making decisions without an accurate idea of what is really going on.
If those metrics haven’t been realigned with new priorities, processes, and challenges, they will obscure the picture of how well the enterprise is performing.
Knowing how well your organization is doing is always the first strategic mandate.
